gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epoch 24V 100Ah (B24100A-C, $1,199, listed out of stock on Epoch's US page) talks only to Epoch's Bluetooth app and has no Victron/CAN/RS485 link, with a limit of 2 in series or 4 in parallel, and that Victron's own battery compatibility list names BattleBorn but not LiTime, Epoch or Redodo, so LiTime ComFlex's 'Victron compatible' claim comes from LiTime, not Victron.
standout_why: I compared against the cited solarpoweredproject.com 100Ah brand comparison (12V models only; its checklist mentions series/parallel limits but gives no numbers and says nothing about Victron or inverter communication) and LiTime's 'Best Victron-Compatible LiFePO4 Battery' guide, which was in ChatGPT's results (it covers 12V models only and has only a general line that 'absence from a published compatibility list does not prove that a battery cannot work electrically'). The cited LiTime 24V Bluetooth product page returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I couldn't check it. None of the pages I opened say that Epoch's 24V 100Ah has no inverter communication, give its 2S/4P limit, or say which brands Victron's own list names.
decides: This changes the 'premium' pick. ChatGPT's $1,199 Epoch 24V 100Ah is out of stock on Epoch's US store and can't feed state of charge or charge limits to a Victron GX. It's a marine/trolling battery with heating and IP67, not a pick for a networked solar or inverter system. For a Victron bank, the only 24V 100Ah with closed-loop communication in ChatGPT's answer is LiTime's ComFlex. LiTime says GX-managed banks go up to 16 in parallel on the BMS-Can port, but Victron has not listed or tested it, so the page should say support comes from LiTime. Redodo's and LiTime's standard Bluetooth 24V models are open-loop: the charger and inverter must be programmed by hand.

findings.label: Series/parallel limit
findings.value: Up to 2 in series (48 V) or up to 4 in parallel (400 Ah at 24 V); mixed series-parallel not addressed

findings.label: Communication
findings.value: Bluetooth to the Epoch Li-Ion app (iOS/Android) only; the page lists no Victron, CAN or RS485 communication
findings.note: Epoch's Victron-comms 24V model is the 24V 230Ah V2 Elite (seen in search listings, not opened).

findings.label: Price and stock
findings.note: Epoch's US store. A recertified unit with a 2-year warranty is sold separately.

findings.label: Charger requirement
findings.value: Max charge 29.2 V; bulk/absorption 28.4–29.2 V; equalization and temperature compensation disabled; recommended charge 50 A; 'Avoid 12V chargers and non-programmable lead-acid chargers'; heating runs on incoming charge current
findings.note: The page gives float as 26.8–27.6 V in the specs but 'lithium-compatible float or disabled' elsewhere.

findings.label: Stated exclusion
findings.value: Deep-cycle battery; for engine starting or alternator-direct charging, 'confirm compatibility directly with Epoch and the equipment manufacturer before installation'
findings.note: BMS: 120 A continuous, 200 A for 60 s.

findings.label: Victron battery compatibility list
findings.value: Lists BattleBorn as tested; LiTime, Epoch, Redodo and SOK are not named. Unlisted third-party batteries 'will require additional information and support from a local supplier'
findings.note: Text search of the raw export for LiTime, Li Time, Epoch, Redodo, Battle and SOK. Only 'BattleBorn' matched. The page says most managed batteries connect via BMS-Can on a GX device.

findings.label: Victron hookup and parallel limit with communication
findings.value: RJ45 cable from the battery's CAN port to the GX BMS-Can port; on the VE.Can port set the profile to 'CAN-bus BMS (500 kbit/s)'; up to 16 batteries in parallel managed by the GX as one bank
findings.note: The guide is written around the 12V 100Ah ComFlex, and its 16-battery example works out to 20,480 Wh. It doesn't say whether the 24V ComFlex follows the same limit or whether communication works with batteries in series. I couldn't open the 24V ComFlex product page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: LiTime's own caveat on Victron listing
findings.value: 'absence from a published compatibility list does not prove that a battery cannot work electrically'; parallel limit stated as 16P1S with communication, 4P4S in standard installs (12V 320Ah model)
findings.source_title: Best Victron-Compatible LiFePO4 Battery: 4 Brands Compared – LiTime
findings.note: The page is dated Nov 12, 2026 and covers 12V models only.
